content_of_post_to_comment:
At the start of last month, I had an objective of going to bed on time every night of September. A very ambitious goal for someone who struggles of bedtime procrastination, but I was committed and motivated.

Everything went according to plan until the last week of the month when I started to feel this is done and I achieved my goal. Then I started to feel like it doesn’t matter, I already made it when in reality I did not. I know it’s silly to have such a goal because building a habit doesn’t work like this (and btw I’m very proud of myself for the 27 nights), but it still bothers me that the month wasn’t perfect like I hoped for. So to the question: how to stick committed to my goals when it feels like I almost already made it?
comment: I think part of the problem is treating the last few nights as a test of whether you succeeded, rather than just more nights of practicing the habit. After 27 nights, you’ve already proved you can do it. Maybe next time, plan for the final few nights to feel less exciting and decide in advance what you’ll do when that “I’ve basically made it” feeling kicks in. That’s probably when the habit needs you most.
